title: Smithsonian's American Latino Museum Gets a Permanent Home
summary:
For six years, the National Museum of the American Latino has existed without a building of its own. Now that is about to change.

In August, the Smithsonian's Board of Regents voted to give the museum a permanent home in the Arts and Industries Building. This 145-year-old landmark sits on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. The Smithsonian already owns the building, so it can move ahead without asking Congress to approve a new site. President Trump has criticized the Smithsonian and proposed cutting funding for the museum, and using an existing building avoids a possible political fight.

Jorge Zamanillo is the museum's founding director. He told PBS NewsHour that people worked for more than 30 years to create the museum, with support from both political parties. They felt Latinos were not well represented in Smithsonian museums or in museums across the country. In December 2020, a law was passed creating the museum to help people understand Latino culture and the impact Latinos have had in the United States.

Zamanillo said the building is symbolic because it is right at the heart of the Mall. He said the museum could expand the building and even double its space. The Arts and Industries Building was the Smithsonian's first national museum, opening in 1881, and it will now also be home to the Smithsonian's newest museum.

He explained that Latinos are not all the same. The museum wants to show the shared experiences and many different stories of Latinos across centuries of American history.

When asked about political pressure, Zamanillo said the museum always goes back to scholarship and facts. When his team meets people around the country, they do not ask about religion or politics. Instead, they look for meaningful stories and objects to collect.
why_it_matters: National museums shape how Americans learn their shared history, and this decision gives Latino history a lasting place at the center of the National Mall.

background_read: The Smithsonian Institution is a group of national museums and research centers, many of them along the National Mall in Washington, D.C.
The National Mall is a long park lined with museums and monuments, and it is one of the most visited places in the country.
Congress passes laws to create new national museums, and finding and paying for a building can take many years.
The National Museum of the American Latino was created to share the history, culture and contributions of Latinos in the United States.
